targets.authors: Schmidt, PJ, Nieman, LK, Danaceau, MA, et al.
targets.title: Differential behavioral effects of gonadal steroids in women with and in those without premenstrual syndrome.
targets.evidence_quote: We evaluated differences between cohorts, attempted to replicate our original findings of a differential behavioral sensitivity to otherwise similar changes in ovarian steroids in women with PMDD compared to healthy comparison women (3), and examined several as yet unanswered questions about the effects of ovarian steroids on symptoms in these women.
targets.outcome_quote: This confirms and replicates our original finding that women with PMDD and healthy comparison women who do not have PMDD have different behavioral responses to the same physiological exposures to both estradiol and progesterone, a phenomenon that, in this experimental paradigm, distinguishes women with PMDD from women without.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly state that the differential hormone sensitivity finding was confirmed and replicated. Progesterone-specific irritability/mood-swings dissociation is framed as an extension newly detectable in the enlarged sample, while the central reproduction of the behavioral phenotype receives an overall affirmative verdict.

reasoning: Independent second cohort augments retained original cohort; new participants re-test the published 1998 differential behavioral sensitivity finding. Other cited hormone studies are background rather than separately identified targets.
